questions.q: A force $\mathrm{F}=\alpha+\beta \mathrm{x}^2$ acts on an object in the x -direction. The work done by the force is 5 J when the object is displaced by 1 m . If the constant $\alpha=1 \mathrm{~N}$ then $\beta$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$F=\alpha+\beta x^2$
Work done $\int d w=\int F \cdot d x$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \Delta W=\int F \cdot d x=\int\left(\alpha+\beta x^2\right) d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \Delta W=\left|\alpha x+\frac{\beta x^3}{3}\right|_0^1=\alpha+\frac{\beta}{3}=5
\end{aligned}$$
Given $\alpha=1$
So, $\frac{\beta}{3}=4\Rightarrow \beta=12 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$

questions.q: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended by a light string of length $L$. It is imparted a minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point $A$ such that it just completes half circle reaching the top most position $B$. The ratio of kinetic energies $\dfrac{( K . E . {)}_{A}}{( K . E . {)}_{B}}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The velocity given is minimum, just enough to complete verticle circle. At the top most point, tension of the string will be zero and gravitational force will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

$mg = \dfrac{m\left({V}_{H}\right)2}{L} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m\left({V}_{H}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2}gL$

Apply energy conservation between point $A$ and $B$, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{V}_L^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{V}_H^{2} + mg ( 2L )$

$⇒ {V}_{L} = \sqrt{5gL}$

Also, ${V}_{H} = \sqrt{gL}$

Required ratio, $\dfrac{( K . E{)}_{A}}{( K . E{)}_{B}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m ( \sqrt{5gL}{)}^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}m ( \sqrt{gL}{)}^{2}} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$~is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$~such that its centripetal acceleration ${a}_{c}$ is varying with time $t$~as ${a}_{c} = k^{2}rt^{2}$ , where $k$& is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the force acting on it is -
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
{a}_{c} = k^{2}rt^{2}$

Or $\dfrac{v2}{r} = k^{2}rt^{2}$~ Or~ $v = krt$
Therefore, tangential acceleration, ${a}_{t} = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = kr$

Therefore, tangential force,~${F}_{t} = m{a}_{t} = mkr$

Only tangential force does work.

$\text{Power} = {F}_{t}v = \left(mkr\right)\left(krt\right)$~$\text{⇒Power} =mk^{2}r^{2}t

$$

questions.q: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $\vec{F}=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) N$. The power generated by the force at time $t$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=(2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \mathrm{N} \\ & \mathrm{m}=1000 \mathrm{gm}=1 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~F}}=m \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{j} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 t \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \mathrm{t}^2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}\end{aligned}$
$\vec{v}=t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}$
Power, $\mathrm{P}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$
$\begin{aligned} & P=\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) \cdot\left(t^2 \hat{i}+t^3 \hat{j}\right) \\ & P=\left(2 t^3+3 t^5\right) W\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moves in a circular orbit~under the central potential field, $U\left(r\right) = \dfrac{- C}{r}$,~where $C$ is a positive constant. The correct radius - velocity graph of the particle's motion is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$U = - \dfrac{C}{r}$

$F = - \dfrac{dU}{dr} = - \dfrac{C}{r2}$

\left|F\right| = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$

$\dfrac{C}{r2} = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$

$v^{2} ∝ \dfrac{1}{r}$

$

questions.q: A particle of mass $500g$ is moving in a straight line with velocity $v = bx\dfrac{5}{2}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $x = 0$~to $x = 4m$ is ~(Take $b = 0 . 25m\dfrac{- 3}{2}s^{- 1}$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the work-energy theorem, work done by all forces will be is equal to the change in kinetic energy.

${W}_{all} = \Delta K$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}mb^{2}\left({x}_{2}^{5} - {x}_{1}^{5}\right)= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 5 \times \dfrac{1}{16} \times {4}^{5} = 16J$

questions.q:
Water falls from a $40m$ high dam at the rate of $9 \times {10}^{4}kg$ per hour. Fifty percentage of gravitational potential energy can be converted into electrical energy. Using this hydro electric energy number of $100W$ lamps, that can be lit, is
(Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since& $50 %$~efficiency is given, half of~the energy of the falling water will be used by the bulbs. Therefore,

$\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{∆ mgh}{\Deltat} = n \times P ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{4}}{3600} \times 10 \times 40 = 100n ⇒ n = 50$

A particle is placed at the point $A$ of a frictionless track $ABC$ as shown in figure. It is gently pushed towards right. The speed of the particle when it reaches the point $B$ is: $($Take \leftg = 10ms^{- 2})$.

$

questions.solution:
Applying conservation of mechanical energy between point $A$ & $B$, we get

$K{E}_{A} + {U}_{A} = K{E}_{B} + {U}_{B}$

$⇒ 0 + mg (1)= \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + mg \times 0 . 5$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{g} = \sqrt{10}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A body of mass 4 kg is placed on a plane at a point P having coordinate $(3,4) \mathrm{m}$. Under the action of force $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) \mathrm{N}$, it moves to a new point Q having coordinates $(6,10) \mathrm{m}$ in 4 sec . The average power and instanteous power at the end of 4 sec are in the ratio of :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \langle\mathrm{p}\rangle=\frac{(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \cdot(3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}})}{4}=6 \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{1}{2} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\frac{3}{4} \hat{\mathrm{j}}\right) \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}} \text { at } \mathrm{t}=4 \mathrm\sec=\left(\frac{1}{2} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\frac{3}{4} \hat{\mathrm{j}}\right) \times 4=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \\ & P_{\text {ins }}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3)(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}})=13 \\ & \frac{\langle\mathrm{P}\rangle}{P_{\text {ins }}}=\frac{6}{13}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ moves on a straight line with its velocity increasing with distance according to the equation $v=\alpha \sqrt{x}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant. The total work done by all the forces applied on the particle during its displacement from $x=0$ to $x=\mathrm{d}$, will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}=\alpha \sqrt{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \text { at } \mathrm{x}=0: \mathrm{v}=0 \\ & & \text { at } \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{d} ; \mathrm{v}=\alpha \sqrt{\mathrm{d}} \\ & \text { W.D }=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}} \\ & \text { W.D }=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(\alpha \sqrt{\mathrm{d}})^2-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(0)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \text { W.D }=\frac{\mathrm{m} \alpha^2 \mathrm{~d}}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle is released from height $S$ above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{V}^2=0+2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{V}^2=2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x})
\end{aligned}$
At B, Potential energy $=m g x$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{mgx}=3 \times \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2 \\ & \mathrm{gx}=\frac{3}{2} \times 2 \mathrm{~g}(\mathrm{~S}-\mathrm{x}) \\ & 4 \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{S} \\ & \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{S}}{4}
\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~g} \times \frac{3 \mathrm{~S}}{4}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{gS}}{2}}$

questions.q: As per the given figure, two blocks each of mass $250g$ are connected to a spring of spring constant $2Nm^{- 1}$. If both are given velocity $v$ in opposite directions, then maximum elongation of the spring is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the maximum elongation of the spring be& $x$.

Using energy conservation

Loss in kinetic energy of both blocks=Gain in spring energy

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} \times 2 = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}$

$⇒ \left(0 . 25\right)v^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times x^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4}v^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times x^{2}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{v}{2}$

questions.q: A force acts on a $2$ kg object so that its position is given as a function of time as $x = 3t^{2} + 5 .$ What is the work done by this force in first $5$ seconds?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here, the position of the object is& $x = 3t^{2} + 5$, therefore the velocity of the object will be,

$v = \dfrac{d x}{d t} = \dfrac{d \left(3t^{2} + 5\right)}{d t}$

$v = 6t + 0$

From the work-energy theorem, all the work done by the force acting on it will be equal to the change in its kinetic energy, i.e.,

$W = KE \left(t = 5s\right) - KE \left($t = 0s\right)$
$W = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$2 $\times \left($6 \times5\right)2 - $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$2 $\times \left($6 \times0\right)2$
$W = 900J$.

$

questions.q: A bullet of mass $200g$ having initial kinetic energy $90J$ is shot inside a long swimming pool as shown in the figure. If it's kinetic energy reduces~to $40J$ within $1s$, the minimum length of the pool, the bullet has& to travel so that it completely comes to rest is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let us assume that the motion of the bullet is of constant retardation inside the water.

Initial kinetic energy& $\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} = 90J$

$⇒ {v}_{0} = 30ms^{- 1}$

Let the retardation is $a$,~then after~$1s$

$\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(30 - a \times 1\right)2 = 40J$

$⇒ 30 - a = 20$

$⇒ a = 10ms^{- 2}$

Stopping distance for the constant retardation is given by,

$l = \dfrac{u2}{2a} = \dfrac{302}{20} = 45m$.

Therefore, the minimum length of the pool required is~$45m$.

questions.q: The potential energy function (in $J$ ) of a particle in a region of space is given as $U =  \left(2x^{2} + 3y^{3} + 2z\right)$. Here $x, y$ and $z$ are in meter. The magnitude of $x$ - component of force (in $N$ ) acting on the particle at point $P ( 1, 2, 3 ) m is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given $U = 2x^{2} + 3y^{3} + 2z$

The expression for the $x -$component of the force can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{F}_{x} & = & - \dfrac{∂ U}{∂ x} \\ & = & - 4x\end{cases}$

Hence, at the point \left(1, 2, 3\right)m$, the value of the force is given by

$\begin{cases}\left|{F}_{x}\right| & = & \left|- 4 \times 1\right|N \\ & = & 4N\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Potential energy as a function of $r$~is given by $U = \dfrac{A}{r10} - \dfrac{B}{r5}$, where $r$~is the interatomic distance, $A$ and $B$ are positive constants. The equilibrium distance between the two atoms will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given& $U = \dfrac{A}{r10} - \dfrac{B}{r5}$.

Now, for equilibrium,~$\dfrac{d U}{d r} = 0$.

So, differentiating the given equation,

$\dfrac{- 10A}{r11} + \dfrac{5B}{r6} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{10A}{r11} = \dfrac{5B}{r6} ⇒ r^{5} = \dfrac{2A}{B} ⇒ r = \left(\dfrac{2A}{B}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.q: A block of mass $m,$ lying on a smooth horizontal surface, is attached to a spring (of negligible mass) of spring constant $k .$ The other end of the spring is fixed, as shown in the figure. The block is initially at rest in its equilibrium position. If now the block is pulled with a constant force $F,$ the maximum speed of the block is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When block attains maximum speed net force on $m$ is zero. $∴ F = kx$

Or $x = \dfrac{F}{k}$

From work energy theorem

$- \dfrac{1}{2}k\left(\dfrac{F}{k}\right)2 + F\left(\dfrac{F}{k}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m{V}_\max^{2}$

$\dfrac{F^{2}}{2k} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{V}_\max^{2}$

${V}_\max = \sqrt{\dfrac{F}{km}}$

questions.q: A force $\overset{→}{F} = \left(2 + 3x\right)\overset{^}{i}$ acts on a particle in the $x$ direction where $F$ is in Newton and $x$ is in meter. The work done by this force during a displacement from $x = 0$~to $x = 4m$~is _____~$J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the work done by a variable force is given by

$W = {∫}_{x1}^{x2}Fdx . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

$\begin{cases}W & = & {∫}_{0}^{4} ( 2 + 3x ) dx \\ & = & {2x + \dfrac{3}{2}x^{2}}_{0}^{4} \\ & = & [ 8 + 24 ] J \\ & = & 32J\end{cases}$

questions.q: Two solids $A$ and $B$ of mass $1$ kg and $2$ kg respectively are moving with equal linear momentum. The ratio of their kinetic energies \left(K . E .\right)A: \left(K . E .\right)B$ will be $\dfrac{A}{1},$~so the value of $A$ will be _________.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy& $K = \dfrac{P2}{2m}, \left({P}_{A} = {P}_{B}\right)

$K ∝ $\dfrac{1}{m}

\dfrac{KA}{KB} = \dfrac{mB}{mA}

$= \dfrac{2}{1}$

$

questions.q:
A block of mass $5$ kg starting from rest pulled up on a smooth incline plane making an angle of $30 °$ with horizontal with an effective acceleration of $1ms^{- 2}$. The power delivered by the puling force at $t = 10s$ from the start is _____~$W$.
[Use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
(Calculate the nearest integer value)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following free-body diagram:

From the above diagram, it can be written that

$F - mgsin30 ° = ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the force applied on the block.

$\begin{cases}F - 50\sin 30 ° & = & 5 \times1 \\ & ⇒ & F = \left(5 + 25\right)N \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 30N\end{cases}$$

The velocity of the block~ \left(v\right)$~at~$t = 10s$~can be written as

$\begin{cases}v & = & 0 + 1ms^{- 2} \times10s \\ & = & 10ms^{- 1}\end{cases}$

Hence, the required power is given by

$\begin{cases}P & = & Fv \\ & = & 30N \times10ms^{- 1} \\ & = & 300W\end{cases}$

questions.q: A $0 . 5kg$ block moving at a speed of $12\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ compresses a spring through a distance $30$ cm when its speed is halved. The spring constant of the spring will be _____~${Nm}^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: Mass of the block& $m = 500g$, initial velocity of the block~$u = 12ms^{- 1}$, and final velocity of the block~$v = \dfrac{u}{2} = 6ms^{- 1}$.

As~non-conservative~forces are not acting on the system we can conserve energy.

Thus, loss in kinetic energy of block~=~Gain in potential energy of spring

$\dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 5 \times {12}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0 . 5 \times {6}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}k \times 0 . {3}^{2}$

$k = 600Nm^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two persons $A$ and $B$ perform same amount of work in moving a body through a certain distance $d$ with application of forces acting at angles $45 °$ and $60 °$ with the direction of displacement respectively. The ratio of force applied by person $A$ to the force applied by person $B$ is $\dfrac{1}{x} .$~The value of $x$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Given,& ${W}_{1} = {W}_{2}$~and, we know that work done is a scalar quantity it means,~${F}_{1}Scos45 ° = {F}_{2}Scos60 °⇒ \dfrac{F1}{F2} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{x}⇒ x = 2$.
